Punitive

PYOO-nih-tiv -- stress on the first syllable, PYOO. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Punitive is intended as punishment.

The new late-work policy felt punitive rather than helpful, docking a full letter grade for each missing day.

Worked Example

After one student forgets his gym clothes, the coach cancels the entire class's game day and assigns everyone extra laps for a week.

The coach's response is punitive -- it exists to punish, not to teach or to fix the problem. Punitive describes actions, rules, or penalties whose purpose is punishment.

How Punitive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disciplinary

disciplinary: intended to enforce rules or correct behavior

retaliatory

retaliatory: done in revenge or response to an injury

penal

penal: relating to punishment, especially under the law

Antonyms

lenient

lenient: mild and merciful rather than harsh

rehabilitative

rehabilitative: intended to restore or reform rather than punish

How Strong Is It? — disciplinary → punitive → retaliatory

disciplinary vs. punitive

disciplinary vs. punitive: Disciplinary is milder and more constructive than punitive -- disciplinary measures aim to correct behavior and teach, while punitive measures exist first and foremost to make the offender pay a penalty.

retaliatory vs. punitive

retaliatory vs. punitive: Retaliatory is harsher than punitive: a punitive penalty punishes within a system of rules, while a retaliatory act strikes back to injure, driven by revenge rather than justice.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pun

Root — pun: penalty, punishment (from Latin punire, 'to punish,' itself from poena, 'penalty')

Suffix — -itive

Suffix — -itive: having the quality of (Latin -ivus; the linking -it- comes from the Latin stem)

Put it together

Put it together: Pun ('penalty, punishment' — from Latin punire, itself from poena, 'penalty') + -itive ('having the quality of'): something punitive has the quality of a penalty — its whole purpose is to make wrongdoing cost something.

Use the root in a new word: impunity

Use the root in a new word: impunity: For years the smugglers operated with impunity, certain no patrol boat would ever reach their cove.

Root Check

Word Choice

Punitive is the formal adjective of punishment: punitive damages, punitive measures, punitive tariffs. Calling a rule punitive often carries criticism -- it hints that the penalty is harsher than necessary and exists to punish rather than to fix anything.
